findings.title: Governing Law
findings.deviation: The governing law is the laws of the Federal Republic of Germany, which is not acceptable as AtliQ Inc only contracts with US clients. The correct governing law should be the laws of India (Pvt Ltd).
findings.impact: This deviation could lead to legal disputes being heard in a jurisdiction that is not favorable to AtliQ Inc.
findings.quote: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the Federal Republic of Germany, excluding the UN Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods (CISG).
findings.counterPosition: The laws of India (Pvt Ltd) should govern the agreement.
findings.linkedQuote: Laws of India (Pvt Ltd) / the relevant US state (Inc); arbitration seated in India or a neutral seat.

findings.title: Limitation of Liability
findings.deviation: AtliQ's liability is unlimited, which is not acceptable. The liability should be capped at 1× fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim, with carve-outs for fraud, wilful misconduct, and breach of confidentiality.
findings.impact: AtliQ could be held liable for significant damages that exceed the agreed-upon cap, leading to financial risk.
findings.quote: The Parties shall be liable without limitation for damage caused intentionally or by gross negligence, for injury to life, body or health, and under the Product Liability Act (Produkthaftungsgesetz).
findings.counterPosition: Mutual cap of 1× fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim; carve-outs limited to fraud, wilful misconduct, and breach of confidentiality.
findings.linkedQuote: Mutual cap of 1× fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim; carve-outs limited to fraud, wilful misconduct and breach of confidentiality; data-protection liability under a separate super-cap (e.g. 2× fees).

findings.title: Indemnity
findings.deviation: The indemnity clause does not fully align with the playbook. It does not exclude AtliQ's own negligence and does not cap the indemnity. The indemnity should be mutual and exclude AtliQ's own negligence.
findings.impact: AtliQ could be required to indemnify the client for its own negligence, which is not acceptable.
findings.quote: Each Party shall indemnify the other against third-party claims resulting from its culpable breach of this Agreement.
findings.counterPosition: Each party indemnifies the other for third-party claims caused by its own breach or negligence; no indemnity for losses caused by the indemnified party's own negligence; indemnities subject to the liability cap (IP infringement excepted).
findings.linkedQuote: Each party indemnifies the other for third-party claims caused by its own breach or negligence; no indemnity for losses caused by the indemnified party's own negligence; indemnities subject to the liability cap (IP infringement excepted).

findings.title: Intellectual Property
findings.deviation: AtliQ retains ownership of PipeKit, which is not acceptable. AtliQ should grant a non-exclusive, perpetual, royalty-free licence to use PipeKit as part of the deliverables.
findings.impact: AtliQ could be required to transfer ownership of PipeKit to the client, which is not in line with AtliQ's standard practice.
findings.quote: Supplier shall deliver the services using its proprietary data-pipeline accelerator 'PipeKit', comprising reusable ingestion connectors, transformation templates, data quality rule libraries and orchestration modules. PipeKit shall be incorporated into the Work Results to reduce implementation time and cost.
findings.counterPosition: Client owns deliverables created specifically for it upon payment; AtliQ retains background IP and grants a non-exclusive, perpetual, royalty-free licence to use it as part of the deliverables.
findings.linkedQuote: Client owns deliverables created specifically for it upon payment; AtliQ retains background IP and grants a non-exclusive, perpetual, royalty-free licence to use it as part of the deliverables.

findings.title: Termination
findings.deviation: The termination clause does not provide for payment for all services performed up to termination, including work in progress. The termination should be mutual with a notice period.
findings.impact: AtliQ could be left with unpaid work in progress if the client terminates the agreement, which is not acceptable.
findings.quote: The right of either Party to terminate for good cause (aus wichtigem Grund) remains unaffected. Good cause exists in particular if the other Party materially breaches its obligations and fails to remedy the breach within thirty (30) days of written notice. Upon termination by Client for convenience (§ 648 BGB), Supplier shall be entitled to the agreed remuneration for services rendered plus compensation for committed costs.
findings.counterPosition: Payment for all services performed up to termination, including work in progress and committed costs; mutual notice period.
findings.linkedQuote: Payment for all services performed up to termination, including work in progress and committed costs; mutual notice period.

fine.note: Payment terms are acceptable as invoices are payable within 30 days of receipt.
Data protection provisions are acceptable as a Data Processing Agreement (DPA) is to be signed before any personal data moves, and the DPA includes the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs).
Set-off is not applicable as the agreement does not allow for it.
There are no restrictive covenants in the agreement.
Insurance provisions are acceptable as the required insurance types and limits are not specified in the document.
